home.heroSubtitleLine2: we help you plan every anime pilgrimage from screen to reality.
home.mapHubSubtitle: Start with the map overview, then dive into anime, cities, and resources for execution details.
home.mapHubPrimaryDesc: Filter by anime, city, and landmark in seconds, then share the same map state with your travel mates.

home.starterStep1Desc: Start from the anime index and check published routes and related posts for that work.
home.starterStep2Desc: Use city hubs to cluster routes by area and choose an itinerary that fits your schedule.

home.starterStep3Desc: Copy route or spot links from Resources so you can open maps quickly during the trip.
home.appPromoDescriptionLine2: Carry the magic of anime in your pocket, ready to depart anytime.
home.faqSectionSubtitle: Have more questions? Reach us anytime via the contact links in the footer.
home.faqA1: An anime pilgrimage means traveling to the real-world locations that appear in anime. SeichiGo organizes those locations into a searchable spot map — find them by series or by city, then compare the view with the scene yourself.
home.faqQ2: How does the planner build an itinerary?
home.faqA2: Tell it the series you want to visit, how many days you have, and which cities. The planner picks matching spots from the database, groups them by geography into ordered days, then adds transit and meal suggestions — a day-by-day itinerary you can keep adjusting.
home.faqQ3: What can I use for free?
home.faqA3: The spot map, the anime and city indexes, and all pilgrimage guides are free. The planner's free tier generates itineraries of up to 3 days, with transit estimated as straight-line distance and no restaurant recommendations; upgrading to Standard unlocks real transit routing and restaurant picks, for trips of up to 7 days.
home.faqQ4: Where does the spot data come from?
home.faqA4: Spots come from the public anime pilgrimage database Anitabi and from user submissions. We keep syncing updates and correcting coordinates and series mappings; if you spot an error, let us know via the contact links in the footer.
home.faqQ5: Can I edit the itinerary myself?
home.faqA5: Yes. Once an itinerary is generated, tell the planner right on the plan page what to change — swap a spot, reorder, add or drop days — and it adjusts the existing plan. You can also save it and come back to keep editing anytime.

about.heroSubtitleLine2: And pilgrimage is touching the edge of that dream in reality.
about.missionCard1Description: We reject vague "approximate locations." We pursue precise coordinates down to latitude and longitude, comparing anime frames with real-world scenes, missing no detail.
about.missionCard2Description: Guides shouldn't be dry instruction manuals. We insist on refined image-text layouts, making the reading experience itself a beautiful spiritual pilgrimage.
about.missionCard3Description: From transportation plans to optimal shooting positions, we provide step-by-step operational guidance, solving the "how to get there" challenge so your departure is never hesitant.
about.whyParagraph1: Often, when we finish a moving anime and feel the urge to "visit this place," we stop at the tedious information search. Scattered coordinates, blurry screenshots, outdated transit info... these obstacles gradually cool our passion.
about.whyParagraph2: We want to change that. SeichiGo is dedicated to organizing the clearest, most beautiful, and most practical pilgrimage guides. We hope that when you stand at that intersection, you won't need to fumble between apps and web pages, but can look up calmly and say to that scenery:
about.futureDescription: We're developing a mobile app with plans to support offline maps, one-tap navigation, and pilgrimage check-ins.
about.futureDescriptionLine2: Our goal is to put all pilgrimage sites in your pocket, becoming your most reliable companion in breaking the dimensional wall.
about.contactDescription: Whether you've found data errors, want to submit your pilgrimage story, or have business collaboration inquiries, we look forward to hearing from you.
about.pressWhatWeAre: SeichiGo is a route-planning tool and guide site for anime pilgrimage. On top of a global map of 50,000+ locations across 1,500+ anime, the AI planner turns an anime and a number of days into a day-by-day route with transit connections. Available in English, Japanese, and Simplified and Traditional Chinese.
about.pressCiteText: You're welcome to cite our content. Please credit "SeichiGo" and link to the page you're citing.
about.pressCitePhotos: Our own on-location photos may be used for editorial and non-commercial purposes with credit.
about.pressCiteFrames: Anime frames belong to their respective rights holders. We reproduce them only for scene comparison and cannot license further use.
about.pressContact: For press, image requests or questions about our data, contact
